# znancount

> Compute the number of non-`NaN` elements in a one-dimensional double-precision complex floating-point ndarray.

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var znancount = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/znancount' );
```

#### znancount( arrays )

Computes the number of non-`NaN` elements in a one-dimensional double-precision complex floating-point ndarray.

```javascript
var Complex128Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex128' );

var x = new Complex128Vector( [ 1.0, 2.0, NaN, NaN, 3.0, 4.0 ] );

var v = znancount( [ x ] );
// returns 2
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **arrays**: array-like object containing a one-dimensional input ndarray.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   If provided an empty one-dimensional ndarray, the function returns `0`.
-   An element is considered `NaN` if either its real or imaginary component is `NaN`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var bernoulli = require( '@stdlib/random/base/bernoulli' );
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/base/discrete-uniform' );
var filledarrayBy = require( '@stdlib/array/filled-by' );
var Complex128Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex128' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/to-array' );
var znancount = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/znancount' );

function clbk() {
    if ( bernoulli( 0.7 ) > 0 ) {
        return discreteUniform( 0, 100 );
    }
    return NaN;
}

var buf = filledarrayBy( 10*2, 'float64', clbk );
var x = new Complex128Vector( buf.buffer );
console.log( ndarray2array( x ) );

var v = znancount( [ x ] );
console.log( v );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
